constellations.toml:
# A low-Earth-orbit positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) mega-constellation: 5 000
# satellites in four Walker shells, scored as a coverage and dilution-of-precision (DOP) map.
#
# The shells are an illustrative design, not any operator's filing:
#   - 1 600 satellites, Walker delta 1600/32/1 at 550 km and 53 deg;
#   - 1 600 satellites, Walker delta 1600/32/7 at 540 km and 53.2 deg;
#   - 1 000 satellites, Walker delta 1000/20/3 at 570 km and 70 deg;
#   -   800 satellites, Walker star 800/16/1 at 560 km and 97.6 deg (near-polar, planes
#       spread over 180 deg) to fill the high latitudes.
#
# At this size the visibility prefilter matters: each epoch the satellites are sorted by
# sub-satellite latitude and a grid row only tests those within one coverage half-angle of
# it. The `work` block of the result states how many satellite-point pair tests a brute-force
# scan would have made and how many were made. The secular J2 drift of the nodes is on, and
# the tracks are downsampled to 120 satellites.

# share of time with PDOP at or below 3 above a 20 deg mask over two hours. The weak spot the
# map shows is the polar caps: no shell reaches above about 82 deg latitude, so a user near a
# pole sees every satellite on one side of the sky and the vertical geometry degrades. MODELLED: an
# illustrative design, two-body orbits with J2, a spherical Earth, geometry only.

solar.summary: Solar system at 2026-09-28T00:00:00 (JD 2461311.50080 TDB), 18 bodies, observer Earth
solar.toml:
# The whole solar system at one epoch.
#
# Every body the engine knows — the Sun, the eight planets, Pluto, the Moon, Phobos,
# Deimos, Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto and Titan — at 2026-09-28 00:00 UTC: its
# heliocentric position and velocity in the ICRF (International Celestial Reference
# Frame, equatorial J2000), its physical constants (gravitational parameter, radii, J2 — the
# second zonal harmonic — where published, sidereal rotation, International Astronomical
# Union (IAU) pole, its J2000 mean value, and prime meridian at the epoch), the light time and one-way and
# two-way range from the Earth, and an orbit track sampled over one revolution.
# result.json carries enough to draw an interactive solar system.
#
# WHERE THE NUMBERS COME FROM
#   planets  Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) Keplerian elements (Standish and Williams),
#            Table 1 for 1800 AD to 2050 AD
#   Moon     the Montenbruck & Gill lunar series, splitting the Earth-Moon barycentre
#   moons    JPL mean elements with the IAU synchronous rotation rate; Titan from the IAU
#            rotation model
#   light    the radiometric light-time solve, transmitter at its retarded position
#
# WHAT IS VALIDATED, AND WHAT IS NOT
# Each body carries its own label. Mercury to Saturn and the Earth are VALIDATED against
# JPL Horizons (Development Ephemeris DE441) within twice the Standish page's nominal
# error. Uranus and Neptune from Table 1 exceed the page's figures against DE441 (by 2.0
# and 5.2 times) and are MODELLED; so are Pluto, the Moon and the seven moons, which
# were measured against Horizons but have no published bound. See tests/solar_system_horizons_reference.rs.
#
# The three links below add the Mars-to-Jupiter, Saturn-to-Earth and Europa-to-Jupiter
# light times: interplanetary relay geometry, a ringed-planet downlink and a moon-to-planet
# hop.
kind = "solar-system"
epoch = "2026-09-28T00:00:00"
observer = "Earth"
track_points = 180

[[links]]
from = "Mars"
to = "Jupiter"

[[links]]
from = "Saturn"
to = "Earth"

[[links]]
from = "Europa"
to = "Jupiter"
solar.frame: ICRF (equatorial J2000), heliocentric; metres, metres per second
solar.label: MIXED: each body carries its own label. Planet positions are VALIDATED against JPL Horizons within twice the Standish nominal error (Mercury to Saturn and the Earth from Table 1; all eight planets from Tables 2a/2b); Uranus and Neptune from Table 1, Pluto, the Moon and the seven moons are MODELLED. Light times are Newtonian, from the same positions.

Europa.summary: Positioning around Europa — surface user, 12 relays at 4500 km, 171 epochs
Europa.toml:
# Positioning a lander on Europa: the Jovian-moon case.
#
# A lander at 20 deg north, 60 deg east on Europa's surface navigates for one Europan day
# (3.55 Earth days, the synchronous rotation period) with twelve navigation satellites at
# 4 500 km in three planes inclined 55 deg, under a 10 deg elevation mask, and a two-way
# range from Earth whenever the Earth is above the lander's horizon. Europa is tidally
# locked, so from a fixed site Jupiter never moves in the sky, while the Earth, riding
# with Jupiter, rises and sets once per Europan day: the Earth link is available only for
# part of the run, and the report shows what the local constellation must carry alone.
#
# The Europa constants (gravitational parameter, mean radius, International Astronomical
# Union (IAU) pole and prime meridian)
# are the published values cited in src/body.rs; no J2 (second zonal harmonic) is carried
# for Europa, so the relay
# orbits are two-body. The Earth-Europa light time is about 36 minutes one way at this
# epoch, near a Jupiter opposition.
#
# One simplification matters more here than at Mars: the relays orbit inside Europa's Hill
# sphere (about 13 700 km) but Jupiter's pull on them is not modelled, so their orbits are
# idealised. The run shows the geometry and what the Earth link adds (availability rises
# from about half the Europan day to about three quarters), not a flyable design.
#
# MODELLED: the constellation, the noise and the measurement model are modelling choices.
kind = "body-pnt"
body = "Europa"
epoch = "2027-02-19T00:00:00"
duration_s = 306822.0
step_s = 1800.0
seed = 11

[user]
kind = "surface"
lat_deg = 20.0
lon_deg = 60.0

[constellation]
planes = 3
sats_per_plane = 4
altitude_km = 4500.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
sigma_range_m = 1.0
mask_deg = 10.0

[earth_link]
enabled = true
sigma_range_m = 1.0
Europa.label: MODELLED: two-body relay orbits with J2 secular drift, geometric visibility, Gaussian range noise and an instantaneous measurement model around a body from the published constants; not validated against a mission's navigation data. The Earth-to-body geometry inherits the solar-system ephemeris labels.

Mars.summary: Positioning around Mars — orbiter user, 12 relays at 10000 km, 296 epochs
Mars.toml:
# Positioning a low Mars orbiter with a Mars navigation constellation and a deep-space link.
#
# A 300 km near-polar orbiter navigates around Mars for one sol (88 775 s) from the
# 2027-02-19 opposition, when the Earth is closest and far from a solar conjunction. Two
# kinds of measurement:
#
#   1. ONE-WAY PSEUDORANGES from twelve navigation satellites at 10 000 km in three planes
#      inclined 60 deg (a Walker delta, phasing 1), flown as two-body orbits with the secular
#      drift from Mars' J2 (the second zonal harmonic, its oblateness). The user clock is
#      unknown, so these rows carry a clock column.
#   2. A TWO-WAY RANGE FROM EARTH, clock-free, whenever the Earth is above the Mars limb
#      for the orbiter. The Earth's direction and distance come from the analytic
#      solar-system ephemeris at every epoch.
#
# The report gives, per epoch, the relays in view, the constellation-only dilution of
# precision, the formal position uncertainty with and without the Earth row, and the
# error of a seeded least-squares fix each way; over the sol, the availability and the
# root-mean-square errors, and the Earth-Mars light time and round trip.
#
# MODELLED. The relay orbits, the 1 m range noise and the instantaneous measurement model
# are modelling choices; nothing here is validated against a mission's navigation data.
# The Mars constants are the published values cited in src/body.rs.
kind = "body-pnt"
body = "Mars"
epoch = "2027-02-19T00:00:00"
duration_s = 88775.0
step_s = 300.0
seed = 7

[user]
kind = "orbiter"
altitude_km = 300.0
inclination_deg = 93.0

[constellation]
planes = 3
sats_per_plane = 4
altitude_km = 10000.0
inclination_deg = 60.0
sigma_range_m = 1.0

[earth_link]
enabled = true
sigma_range_m = 1.0

The Earth-to-body geometry inherits the solar-system ephemeris labels.

sweep.summary: campaign 46aa07cb58fb | Jammer power sweep: availability and J/S against transmit power | sweep of `jamming`: 13 nodes over [jammer_power] | 13 member runs (MODELLED)
sweep.toml:
# A parameter sweep through a campaign: the jamming example's receiver (52 N, 4 E,
# GPS-like 24-satellite Walker shell) under a broadband jammer 1 km away, with the
# jammer's transmit power swept from -50 dBW (10 nW) to +10 dBW (10 W) in 5 dB
# steps. Each node is an ordinary `jamming` run; the campaign records, per node,
# the fraction of epochs with at least four satellites still tracking, the mean
# jammer-to-signal ratio (J/S), and the fewest satellites tracking.
#
# The jamming chain (Kaplan and Hegarty, Understanding GPS/GNSS, 3rd ed., section
# 9.4) is deterministic, so one run per node is the whole answer; add `runs` and a
# `seed_key` to make every node a Monte Carlo ensemble for a stochastic kind.
# J/S moves exactly 1 dB per dB of transmit power; availability falls from 1 to 0
# where the effective carrier-to-noise density ratio crosses the 25 dB-Hz floor.

monte.summary: campaign e093a8c2f169 | Monte Carlo: free-running clock error against its closed form | monte carlo of `clock`: 200 seeds | 200 member runs (MODELLED)
monte.toml:
# A seeded Monte Carlo ensemble through a campaign, on a case with a closed form.
#
# A chip-scale atomic clock (Microchip SA.45s datasheet sigma_y(1 s) = 3e-10, so a
# white-frequency-noise intensity q_wf = 9e-20 s^2/s and nothing else stochastic) is
# disciplined to GNSS for 600 s and then coasts to 3600 s. The holdover predictor
# removes the deterministic frequency offset exactly, so the time error at the end
# of the run is the accumulated white-frequency noise since the last synchronisation
# at 590 s: Gaussian, mean zero, variance q_wf * tau with tau = 3010 s, a standard
# deviation of sqrt(9e-20 * 3010) s = 16.46 ns (NIST Technical Note 1337, the random
# walk of phase under white frequency noise).
#
# Realisation k runs the scenario with `seed = 42 + k`, so the ensemble reproduces
# exactly. The campaign reports, per metric, the mean, the standard deviation, the
# 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles and a fixed-seed bootstrap 95% confidence interval
# on the mean. The test suite checks that the mean falls inside that interval around
# zero and that the spread matches 16.46 ns.
#
# MODELLED: the clock is a datasheet-level model, not a measurement of any unit.
kind = "campaign"
title = "Monte Carlo: free-running clock error against its closed form"
seed = 20260928

[monte_carlo]
runs = 200
seed_key = "seed"
metrics = [
  { name = "final_error", path = "classical.series[-1].error_ns" },
  { name = "timing_rms", path = "classical.fom.timing_rms_ns" },
]

[monte_carlo.scenario]
seed = 42
threshold_ns = 20.0
[monte_carlo.scenario.time]
step_s = 10.0
duration_s = 3600.0
[monte_carlo.scenario.gnss]
windows = [
  { t0 = 0.0, t1 = 600.0, state = "nominal" },
  { t0 = 600.0, t1 = 3600.0, state = "denied" },
]
[monte_carlo.scenario.clock_quantum]
id = "optical-sr-lattice"
provenance = "Strontium optical lattice clock, space-oriented goal sigma_y(1s)=1e-15 (arXiv:1503.08457); not flown."
y0 = 5.0e-17
q_wf = 1.0e-30
q_rw = 0.0
[monte_carlo.scenario.clock_classical]
id = "csac-sa45s"
provenance = "Microchip SA65 / SA.45s CSAC datasheet sigma_y(1s)=3e-10; q_wf=sigma_y(1s)^2."
y0 = 5.0e-10
q_wf = 9.0e-20
q_rw = 0.0
monte.title: Monte Carlo: free-running clock error against its closed form

compose.summary: campaign 504dd3a57cbc | One jammer, a ship and a car | compose: 2 members | 2 member runs (MODELLED)
compose.toml:
# Cross-domain composition: one jammer, two platforms. A ship in the Gulf of Finland
# (59.80 N, 24.90 E, the maritime-strait-jamming example's receiver) and a car on a
# Helsinki coast road (60.17 N, 24.94 E) sit under the same broadband jammer, placed
# at 59.80 N, 25.44 E, 30 m up (about 30 km from the ship and 50 km from the car).
#
# At 8 dBW (6.3 W) the ship loses every satellite (mean jammer-to-signal ratio,
# J/S, about 39 dB) while the car, 20 km further off, keeps at least four (about
# 35 dB): the combined summary names the ship as the worst platform.
#
# The jammer's power and position are declared once under [[compose.shared]] and
# written into each member at the keys it binds them to, so the two runs cannot

#
# MODELLED: as the `jamming` kind is. The car is modelled with the same open-sky
# receiver as the ship; urban masking and the vehicle antenna are not.
kind = "campaign"
title = "One jammer, a ship and a car"
seed = 20260928

[[compose.shared]]
name = "jammer_power"
unit = "dBW"
value = 8.0

[[compose.shared]]
name = "jammer_position"
unit = "m"
